The repo is essentially empty — a fresh repo with only opencode config. There are no Dockerfiles, no existing workflows. The user wants a GitHub Actions workflow that logs in to a container registry before pushing a Docker image.

Since this is a generic request with no existing project, I'll create a standard workflow. GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io) is the most common default and uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` so no secrets setup required. I'll create `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`.

The workflow: on push to main and tags, log in to ghcr.io using docker/login-action, then build and push using docker/build-push-action (or setup-buildx). This is the canonical pattern.

Let me create it. No need for todos for a single file. I'll make it clean and idiomatic.

Empty repo, so I'll create a standard GHCR publish workflow.

input.content:
name: Docker

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to the container registry
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract metadata (tags, labels)
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build and push image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
